Bird Flu Could Eliminate ThemDwindling vulture populations are locked in a fight for their livesJCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleVultures might not be the most charismatic birds, but they do perform an important job. As carrion-feeding scavengers, they dispose of decaying animal matter, even bones, right down their throats. As part of this garbage collection duty, they also neutralize pathogens, routinely gobbling up tissue that’s festering with rabies, anthrax, and botulism and disposing of it in their highly acidic stomachs. Of course, vultures aren’t entirely invulnerable to infection. With 16 of 23 vulture species already designated as threatened, the H5N1 avian flu could wreak havoc on their dwindling numbers. Now a team of biologists is sounding the alarm about what declining vulture populations could mean for ecosystems (and us) and issuing a call to action in a letter published in Conservation Biology.Read more: “We’ll Miss the Vulture”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
